review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Lean core and Batteries for counterparts to its concept-level definitions: Xor, Fact, Function.swap₂, the Classical.dec* family, existsCases, classicalRecOn, byContradiction', hidden, and the simprocs. Only one real duplication turned up. Mathlib's `Classical.decEq` has the same type and meaning as core's `Classical.typeDecidableEq`, and Mathlib now uses both. `Classical.dec` and `Classical.decPred`/`decRel` are documented shorthands for `propDecidable` and its pointwise forms. Core has no counterpart to them, so they are weaker candidates and I did not report them separately. Core has no `Xor` Prop-level definition (only `XorOp` and `HXor`, which are unrelated), so `Xor` here is fine. Theorem-level duplicates were excluded as the rubric requires. I did not check whether other Mathlib files define their own classical decidability helpers.

findings.excerpt: noncomputable def decEq (α : Sort*) : DecidableEq α := by infer_instance
findings.problem: Core already provides `Classical.typeDecidableEq (α : Sort u) : DecidableEq α`, which is the same noncomputable classical `DecidableEq` for an arbitrary type, built from `propDecidable`. Mathlib's `Classical.decEq` is a second definition of this object with the same type and body. Both are used widely and interchangeably: `Classical.decEq` in DFinsupp and Sym, `Classical.typeDecidableEq` in `Set.decidableEq`, `Submodule.decidableEq`, Determinant, and others. The two names are not definitionally linked by an exported lemma or alias, so users must know which spelling a file expects.
findings.proposed_change: Make `Classical.decEq` a thin alias or abbreviation of the core `Classical.typeDecidableEq`, for example `@[reducible] def decEq := typeDecidableEq`. Add a docstring saying it is the Mathlib short name. Optionally migrate the remaining `Classical.decEq` call sites to the core name and then deprecate it. Keep `dec`, `decPred` and `decRel` as shorthands.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical classical `DecidableEq` definition. The two spellings can no longer diverge, for example in reducibility attributes. Readers do not have to wonder whether two instances produced by the two names are the same.

evidence.excerpt:
noncomputable def typeDecidableEq (α : Sort u) : DecidableEq α :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance
noncomputable instance decidableEq : DecidableEq (Set α) := Classical.typeDecidableEq (Set α)
